To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GPU is the most efficient device to accelerate agent-based simulations, but that the CPU is the most efficient when the number of agents is low.

the performance of the GPGPU application is significantly improved by using the integrated heterogeneous architectures, which can be attributed to two factors: (1) the reduction in the overhead for data transfers between the CPU and the integrated GPU; (2) the improvement in the performance of the CPU and the CPU-GPU synchronization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient programming environment for the execution of agent-based models in heterogeneous systems.
the design, implementation, and evaluation of an automatic mapping of agent-based models to heterogeneous architectures.
the design and implementation of a programming model and a compiler framework to support GPGPU applications on heterogeneous architectures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the most part, GPGPU applications can be accelerated on integrated heterogeneous architectures, but that there is still much room for improvement.
GPGPU applications can be accelerated by a factor of two to four on heterogeneous architectures, but this is highly dependent on the application.
GPGPU programming is not yet ready to replace CPU programming in general-purpose applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new GPGPU programming model and compiler framework that is capable of generating code for heterogeneous architectures, and we have used this framework to develop a new GPGPUSIM framework that is capable to accelerate the simulation of agent-based model on such architectures.
we have developed a new programming model and a compiler for mapping GPGPU programs to heterogeneous architectures.
we have developed a new approach to accelerate the execution of agent-based models (ABMs) on heterogeneous systems, by exploiting both CPU and GPU.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the CPU and the performance of the GPU can be improved by using the other device to accelerate the execution of the application.
the GPU can be effectively exploited for accelerating agent-based models (ABMs), which are widely used to model complex systems in a wide range of scientific and engineering applications.
the performance of agent-based models (ABMs) on heterogeneous architectures can be improved by using GPGPU techniques to exploit the data parallelism in the ABM simulation.
